title: ₹300 Crore, a Zombie Apocalypse, and Ranveer Singh's Wildest Bet Yet — Pralay Heads to Australia
excerpt: India's most expensive standalone film pairs Ranveer with Scam 1992 director Jai Mehta and South sensation Kalyani Priyadarshan for a post-apocalyptic thriller unlike anything Bollywood has attempted
body:
Ranveer Singh has fought wars, played emperors, and danced on top of moving cars. Now he's going to fight zombies in a destroyed Mumbai — and he's spending ₹300 crore to do it.

**Pralay**, the post-apocalyptic zombie thriller that has been gestating in Bollywood's pipeline for months, has locked its shoot for September 2026, with a significant chunk of filming set to take place in **Australia**. According to a Pinkvilla exclusive, pre-production is already underway abroad, with director **Jai Mehta**, Ranveer, and a team of international technicians building the dystopian world from scratch.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=qIQgoAoeM14</youtube>


This isn't just another Bollywood film. This is Ranveer Singh producing for the first time, under his newly minted banner **Ma Kasam Films**, and swinging for the kind of genre storytelling that Indian cinema has historically left to Hollywood.

## The Man Behind the Camera

If **Jai Mehta**'s name sounds familiar, it should. He co-directed *Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story* — the show that turned Pratik Gandhi into an overnight sensation and gave every finance bro in the country a new personality trait. The series swept 11 out of 14 nominations at the Filmfare OTT Awards and its theme music crossed seven million streams.

Pralay marks Jai's feature film directorial debut, and he's chosen to go impossibly big. The film is co-produced by his father **Hansal Mehta**'s True Story Films alongside Ranveer's Ma Kasam Films and **Sameer Nair**'s Applause Entertainment.

When rumours surfaced that Pralay might be an adaptation of José Saramago's novel *Blindness*, Hansal shut them down personally. "It is an original story that was developed by Jai with his co-writer **Vishal Kapoor**," the senior filmmaker told reporters. He'd seen the 2008 Julianne Moore adaptation of Blindness, he added. He wasn't impressed.

## A Married Couple vs. the End of the World

The plot centres on a married couple fighting for survival in a dystopian Mumbai. It's an intimate human drama dressed in the skin of a genre spectacle — the kind of premise that could deliver both spectacle and genuine emotional devastation.

And for the role of the woman fighting alongside Ranveer through the ruins, the makers went south.

**Kalyani Priyadarshan** — daughter of legendary filmmaker Priyadarshan, breakout star of the Malayalam blockbuster *Lokah: Chapter 1 – Chandra* — has been confirmed as the female lead. Reports suggest she was initially hesitant about debuting in such a niche genre, until Ranveer personally called her, walked her through the script's vision, and convinced her to sign on.

It's a calculated pairing. Kalyani brings credibility in the South Indian market and a screen presence that's equal parts vulnerability and steel. Ranveer, fresh off the record-shattering run of **Dhurandhar** and **Dhurandhar 2** (which crossed ₹1,200 crore worldwide), brings the kind of box office muscle that allows a zombie thriller to exist at this scale in India.

## Why It Matters for the Diaspora

Bollywood has flirted with horror. It's dabbled in science fiction. But a ₹300 crore post-apocalyptic zombie epic shot in Australia with international VFX teams? That's new territory. For NRIs who've spent years watching *Train to Busan*, *The Last of Us*, and *28 Days Later* while wondering why Indian cinema wouldn't touch the genre seriously — Pralay is the answer.

The decision to shoot extensively in Australia is telling. It signals that the filmmakers want a production quality indistinguishable from Hollywood genre films — not the green-screen-heavy shortcuts that have plagued Indian VFX-driven cinema in the past. Director Jai Mehta has reportedly planned to merge physical sets with AI-driven visual effects to create a look unlike anything seen in Indian cinema before.

## The Bigger Picture

Ranveer stepping behind the camera as producer suggests a shift in how he sees his career. At his commercial peak — two back-to-back all-time blockbusters, the Don franchise reportedly available to him but set aside — he's choosing to bankroll a debut director's vision in a genre that has zero precedent in Hindi cinema.

That's either visionary or insane. Knowing Ranveer, it's probably both.

Pralay is expected to begin filming in September 2026, with a release likely in late 2027. An official announcement with first-look material is still pending.

In the meantime, somewhere in Australia, they're building a destroyed Mumbai. And Ranveer Singh is getting ready to walk through it.
